svg.title: Trust zones, local and cloud — authority lives in grants, not in text

g.text: Trust zones, local and cloud — authority lives in grants, not in text
The desktop core is the only writer of the vault. AWS services receive consented data, are confined per tenant, and send back only proposals.
1 · Content enters the core as data: parsed, sanitized and rendered in an isolated origin.
2 · Extensions ask the policy broker; a grant (principal + action + scope + expiry) decides.
3 · Only consented, scope-filtered data leaves the device, with a short-lived device JWT.
4 · API handlers assume a tenant-tagged session; IAM, KMS and row-level security confine each tenant.
5 · Agent tools and site builds run isolated, with no route back to devices.
6 · Results come back only as patch proposals the author reviews and the core commits.
7 · Injected text asking for tools or uploads gets nothing: it holds no grant.
